title: Dynamical systems gallery (Draft)
description: Six independent calculations (Lorenz, Mandelbrot, logistic map, Game of Life, Gray–Scott, double pendulum) as Drafts that only share their settings: the Agent's "Generate Cards" hands them to helpers that write them at the same time, a bird each.

cards.summary: Takes size and seed from settings. Solves the Lorenz equations (σ=10, ρ=28, β=8/3) from (1, 1, 1) with RK4 at dt=0.005 for 40000 steps, discarding the first 1000. Projects the orbit on the x–z plane, counts visits on a size×size grid and shows them as a PNG in log shading. σ, ρ, β and the number of steps are parameters. Asserts that the orbit stays within |x|<30 and 0<z<60, and logs the ranges of x and z. Uses numpy and pillow.

cards.summary: Takes size from settings. Splits the complex plane from −2.2 to 0.8 (real) and −1.5 to 1.5 (imaginary) into size×size, counts iterations to divergence up to 200, and shows it as a PNG with smooth colouring (diverged points get a log log |z| correction to their count). The range and the maximum number of iterations are parameters. Asserts that c=0 belongs to the set and c=1+1i does not, and logs the fraction of points in the set. Uses numpy and pillow, with the loop written as numpy array operations.

cards.summary: Takes size from settings. For x_{n+1} = r x_n (1 − x_n), splits r from 2.5 to 4.0 into size values; for each r, starting from x_0=0.5, discards 1000 iterations and plots the next 300 values of x as points on a size×size image with r across and x up, and shows it as a PNG. The range of r and the numbers of iterations are parameters. Asserts that at r=3.2 the values after discarding settle on two values (period 2), and logs those two values. Uses numpy and pillow.

cards.summary: Takes size and seed from settings. Fills a board of size/4 cells per side (a torus joined top to bottom and left to right) at density 0.3 with random numbers by seed, advances Conway's Game of Life 200 generations, and shows the final board as a PNG at 4 pixels per cell. The number of generations and the density are parameters. First asserts that a board with a single glider, advanced 4 generations, moves it one cell diagonally. Logs the first, last and maximum number of live cells per generation. Uses numpy and pillow.

cards.summary: Takes size and seed from settings. On a periodic grid of side size/2, starts from u=1, v=0, sets the central 20×20 to u=0.5, v=0.25 and adds ±1% fluctuations from random numbers by seed. Advances the Gray–Scott model (Du=0.16, Dv=0.08, F=0.035, k=0.065, dt=1, a 5-point Laplacian) 6000 steps, and shows the distribution of v, enlarged 2×, as a PNG. F, k and the number of steps are parameters. Asserts that u and v stay within 0–1 throughout, and logs the mean and maximum of the final v. Uses numpy and pillow, with the loop written as array operations.

cards.summary: Takes size from settings. Solves a double pendulum of length 1, mass 1 and gravity 9.81 for 20 seconds with RK4 at dt=0.001, twice: from θ1=120°, θ2=−10° (at rest), and with θ1 alone shifted by 1e−6 radians. Overlays the paths of the two tips in different colours on a size×size image and shows it as a PNG. The initial angles and the time are parameters. Asserts that the relative error of the first one's mechanical energy is below 1e−4, and logs the time at which the two tips are first more than 0.1 apart.

notes.html: Dynamical systems gallery Each of the six computations takes only settings and depends on no other. The Agent can split them up and write them at the same time (delegate)

intro: Six Drafts that depend on no other. With "Generate Cards" in the app, the Agent splits them among helpers and implements them at the same time.
